sec:
Vote by mail or absentee

Can’t get to your polling place on Election Day? Here is how to vote by mail in West Virginia, from the state’s own election office and its laws. Checked October 21, 2026.

Ask for your ballot by

Wednesday, October 28Passed

Your county clerk must receive your application by Wednesday, October 28, 2026 (the 6th day before the election). The clerk mails your ballot within one business day of getting it. (official page)

Send it back

By mail: your ballot must be postmarked on or before Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, 2026, and reach your county clerk before the count review (canvass) starts on Monday, November 9, 2026. A ballot with no postmark still counts if the mail delivers it by Wednesday, November 4. By hand: it must reach the county clerk's office by Monday, November 2, 2026, the day before the election. (official page)

The last day to ask for a ballot by mail has passed. You can still vote in person, early or on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3.You can still vote in person on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3. Early voting in person runs through Saturday, October 31, 2026. When and where to vote early.

West Virginia’s own page on voting by mail

At school away from home, in West Virginia or in another state? What West Virginia says about students is under Show more.

Who can vote by mail

Yes. You can vote by mail only if you cannot vote in person during early voting or on Election Day for a reason the state accepts. The application lists them: illness, injury or another medical reason that keeps you confined; advanced age or a physical disability; jail or home detention (if not convicted of a felony); work hours and distance from the county seat; the state's Address Confidentiality Program; a polling place you cannot get into because of a disability; personal business or travel; going to college, a university or other schooling or training; serving as a federal or state officer away from your county; or a work assignment of four years or less outside your county. For the travel, school, officer and work-assignment reasons, your ballot must be mailed to an address outside your home county. (official page)

How to ask for a ballot

  • Mail, email or fax. Fill in the state's Absentee Ballot Application in your own handwriting, check your reason, sign it, and mail, fax or email it to your county clerk. You must apply separately for each election. If you sign with a mark, a witness must sign too. If someone helps you because of a disability or because you cannot read, that helper signs an oath on the form. Open it (official page)
  • In person. You can hand-deliver your application to your county clerk's office. Open it (official page)

How to send it back

  • By mail. Mail it back so it is postmarked by Election Day, November 3, 2026. (official page)
  • In person. Bring it to your county clerk's office by Monday, November 2, 2026. Someone else may bring it for you, but no one person may deliver more than two voters' absentee ballots. (official page)

What the envelope needs

If this is your first time voting and you are voting by mail, send a copy of an ID with your ballot that shows your current name and address: a photo ID, a utility bill, bank statement, government check, paycheck or other government document. If you have voted in person in a federal election in West Virginia before, no ID is needed for your absentee ballot. A witness signs the application only if you sign with a mark. (official page)

Track your ballot

Track your ballot on West Virginia’s own site (official page)

Vote early in person instead

Wednesday, October 21, 2026 to Saturday, October 31, 2026.

Early voting runs Wednesday, October 21, through Saturday, October 31, 2026, at the county courthouse, an annex or a community voting location during regular business hours, plus 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on the last two Saturdays (October 24 and October 31). (official page)

Students

At school in West Virginia, away from home

The state's application lists "attendance at college, university, or other place of education or training" as a reason to vote by mail. If you choose it, your ballot must be mailed to an address outside your home county (such as your school address in another county). The state's pages do not speak to whether a student may register at their school address instead. (official page)

At school in another state, with West Virginia as home

The same reason on the application (going to college or other schooling) covers a West Virginia voter at school in another state; the ballot is then mailed to an address outside your home county. The state's pages do not speak to out-of-state students separately. (official page)

Military and overseas

Military voters, their families and U.S. citizens overseas use the Federal Post Card Application (FPCA); a first-time registrant must mail it no later than 21 days before Election Day, and voters already registered may email, fax or mail it to the county clerk. An online request form is also available to them. They send the ballot back the way it was sent to them, or by mail, and it must arrive before the canvass starts (November 9, 2026). (official page)

West Virginia in the Federal Voting Assistance Program’s guide

Good to know

  • West Virginia does not let every voter vote by mail: you must have one of the reasons the state lists.
  • For most voters the request is the paper application; the state's online request form is only for military and overseas voters, voters with disabilities who qualify for an electronic ballot, and first responders called away on duty.
  • The state's general rule on where you vote: register with the address where you live (no P.O. box), and vote where you are a true (bona fide) resident (Elections FAQ; West Virginia Code 3-1-3).
  • The state's absentee pages do not mention drop boxes.
  • If you are in the hospital on Election Day, you or a family member can ask the county clerk for an emergency absentee ballot from October 27 until noon on Election Day. Some counties also offer this to voters who become confined in the county by illness or disability from October 27 on; ask your county clerk.
  • Voters with a physical disability that keeps them from voting in person or by paper ballot, and first responders called away on duty, can ask for a ballot they vote electronically.
